newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures ends up in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures ends up in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up in slow trading on the Shanghai Metal Exchange (SME) on Friday helped by speculative buying by retail investors, traders said.
The most active June 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 23,670 ($2,853), rising 80 yuan. It opened at 23,610 yuan per tonne and hit a low of 23,600 yuan.
March rose 20 to 23,090, April was unchanged at 23,320, May increased 80 to 23,580, July 110 to 23,670 and August 110 to 23,560.
Combined volume fell to 34,170 tonnes from 42,200.
Copper opened little changed and speculative buying pushed the prices slightly up for most of the session, traders said.
They said retail investors continued to dominate trading, with institutions staying on the sidelines given a lack of market moving-news.
"Speculative buying was responsible for the day's rises but most investors were not willing to trade ahead of the weekend, resulting in slow trading," one trader said.
Traders said it was better for investors to stay on the sidelines while the market trend remained unclear.
Aluminium ended mostly down. March rose 20 yuan to 15,920 yuan ($1,919) per tonne, April fell 10 to 16,290, May was down 20 to 16,580 and June fell 50 to 16,800.
Combined volume rose to 4,160 tonnes from 4,120.
